interview.name: Eli
interview.answer: I don’t have the time or place for the repair drive in the notes.

reflections: Eli is willing to help and prefers clear, concrete next steps before committing.
Quinn is acting as a coordinator, relaying information and following up on logistics.
Opal is providing task-specific guidance, and the group is aligning around a practical repair plan.
Eli is the main organizer and prefers clear, simple plans with tasks kept in order.
Opal and Mara help by supplying or relaying specific repair details, while Hana prefers to wait for complete information before acting.
The group is coordinating a repair drive collaboratively, with a shared emphasis on straightforward communication and sequencing.
Eli prefers simple, ordered plans and clear next steps, especially when coordinating with others.
Hana is cautious and detail-oriented, wanting to wait for missing information before proceeding.
Pia and Jules are cooperative coordinators who help keep the process organized and communicate updates promptly.
Eli tends to keep coordination simple, ordered, and explicit, with a strong preference for step-by-step sequencing.
The others generally respond well to Eli’s structure and mirror that same orderly, confirmatory style.
This group appears practical and task-focused, with cooperation built through concise updates and clear role acceptance.

Rey and Jules both respond cooperatively and are willing to follow the existing structure rather than redirect it.

events.text: Quinn: Oh, the repair drive? I’ve already got a few neighbors interested — want me to pass your name along too?
events.speaker: Quinn

events.text: Eli: Yes, please pass my name along. I’d appreciate knowing the time and place so I can plan ahead.
events.speaker: Eli

events.text: Quinn: Absolutely — I’ll let you know as soon as I have the time and place, and I’ll pass your name along right away.
events.speaker: Quinn

events.text: Eli: Let’s keep it simple and set a clear plan for the repair drive. I’m happy to help if you tell me what needs fixing first.
events.speaker: Eli

events.text: Opal: Thanks, Eli — the first stop should be the porch light at Maple and 3rd, then the loose gate latch by the community garden.
events.speaker: Opal

events.text: Eli: That works for me. I’ll start with the porch light at Maple and 3rd, then head to the gate latch by the community garden.
events.speaker: Eli

events.text: Eli: That’s the plan I’ve got: porch light at Maple and 3rd first, then the gate latch by the community garden. If anything else needs fixing, tell me in order and I’ll keep it simple.
events.speaker: Eli

events.text: Mara: Perfect — I’ll keep it in order and let folks know to start with the porch light at Maple and 3rd, then the garden gate latch.
events.speaker: Mara

events.text: Eli: Great, that sounds good to me. Keep me posted if anything else gets added, and I’ll stick to the order.

events.speaker: Pia

events.text: Eli: Thanks, Pia. The address is the same, and 4:30 works for me.
events.speaker: Eli

events.text: Eli: Let’s stick to the list in order: porch light at Maple and 3rd first, then the gate latch by the community garden. If there’s more, just tell me what comes next and I’ll keep it simple.

events.text: Jules: Sounds good — I’ll keep it in order and start with the porch light at Maple and 3rd, then the gate latch by the community garden. If I hear of anything else, I’ll pass it along next.
